title: An outage no longer causes a Nak hot-loop that dead-letters buffered evidence
description: Original bug: Stage 9 consumed the entire offline buffer during a disconnect and Nak'd every item in a tight loop — 55 Naks measured across a ~50s real outage, blowing through JetStream's MaxDeliver=5 and dead-lettering evidence the buffer exists to protect. Fixed by gating queue consumption on websocket.Client.Connected().
preconditions: A queue with one buffered item and a fake sender reporting disconnected
steps: Start the upload component with the sender disconnected
expectedResult: Zero Send attempts occur while disconnected; the buffered item is still present and drains once reconnected.
linkedDefect: VTEC-internal (Task 8.1 live outage test, 55 Naks -> 0 Naks after fix)

title: Container recreation no longer bricks the credential cache
description: Original bug: the cache's device-bound key derivation fell back to os.Hostname(), and Docker defaults a container's hostname to its own container ID, which changes on every recreate — silently corrupting the cache and forcing re-registration with an already-consumed, single-use license key. Fixed with a pinned hostname: in the compose file.
preconditions: A running connector with hostname: pinned in docker-compose.yml
expectedResult: The connector keeps the same connector_id across recreation; no re-registration attempt occurs.

title: The server reads the real 'data'/'compression' fields, not the originally-invented 'ciphertext' field
description: Task 7.3 originally invented ciphertext (and omitted compression) believing no Go-side contract existed yet. internal/pipeline/queue_stage.go's real EvidencePayload struct defines data/compression. Fixed to match field-for-field.
preconditions: A real evidence_upload envelope shaped exactly like the Go connector's EvidencePayload
steps: Send the envelope over a real mTLS WS connection
expectedResult: The server parses data/compression correctly and stores a valid vtec_evidence_uploads document — no schema-mismatch rejection.
linkedDefect: VTEC-internal (ciphertext/data field mismatch, found during Phase 8 wiring)

title: Server-side evidence decryption resolves the key via the real Vault broker, not an orphaned dev key store
description: Original bug: the connector fetched its encryption key via the real Vault-backed credential relay, but the server decrypted using a separate, never-populated DevEvidenceCrypto key map, so every real decryption failed with 'no decryption key configured'. Fixed by resolving through the same Vault broker at the same conventional ref name on both sides.
preconditions: A real evidence upload from a connector whose encryption key lives only in Vault
expectedResult: Decryption succeeds using the Vault-resolved key; no 'no decryption key configured' error occurs.
linkedDefect: VTEC-internal (dev key store gap, Phase 8 first live run)

title: A certificate with an empty-string OrganizationalUnit is rejected, not treated as present
description: pkix.Name{OrganizationalUnit: []string{""}} produces a slice of length 1, so the original len(...)==0 check didn't catch an empty tenant_id. Fixed to also check the first element for an empty string.
preconditions: A certificate with OrganizationalUnit set to a single empty string
expectedResult: An error is returned naming the missing tenant_id — the empty string is not silently accepted.
linkedDefect: VTEC-internal (empty-OU bypass, caught by an added regression test)

title: vtec_adapter_connection_status's target label is the real network endpoint, not a duplicate of the adapter name
description: Original bug: RegisterAdapter(name, adapter) set target=name, collapsing the two labels to the same value and defeating the point of having both.
preconditions: Two adapters with distinct instance names and distinct real targets
expectedResult: adapter and target differ for both entries.

title: RefreshAdapterHealth is actually invoked once per collection cycle in production
description: The series existed since Phase 1 and was unit-tested in isolation, but nothing in main.go ever called it — it had never been populated by a real run. Fixed by wiring it into scheduler.OnResult.
preconditions: A live connector with at least one adapter
expectedResult: The series shows a real, current value for the adapter — not absent from the scrape.
linkedDefect: VTEC-internal (dead code path, found during Task 9.1 scoping)

title: The queue depth series is exported as vtec_queue_depth{queue_name}, matching wiki §16, not the earlier vtec_queue_items_count
preconditions: A queue with one enqueued item
expectedResult: vtec_queue_depth{queue_name="VTEC_EVIDENCE"} appears with the correct count; vtec_queue_items_count does not appear at all.

title: The Go WebSocket/renewal clients reliably present their client certificate via GetClientCertificate
description: A static tls.Config.Certificates list is matched against the server's advertised AcceptableCAs by an internal Go heuristic that can silently send no certificate at all even when a valid one is configured — this never surfaced in Go-vs-Go tests (Go's own DN encoding self-matches) and only appeared in the real cross-language, cross-process run. Fixed by using GetClientCertificate, called unconditionally.
preconditions: A real vtec-management-service TLS server (not a Go test server) and a connector with a valid, correctly-chained client certificate
steps: Connect the real connector to the real server over mTLS
Inspect whether the server actually receives a client certificate
expectedResult: The server receives and verifies the client certificate on every connection attempt, not intermittently.
linkedDefect: VTEC-internal (silent no-cert-sent bug, Task 3.8 first cross-process test)

title: A registration envelope sent immediately after connection open is never silently dropped
description: The server originally attached its 'message' listener only after two awaited DB calls; ws's receiver parses and emits frames as soon as they arrive regardless of listener timing, so an envelope sent right after the client's own 'open' event could arrive with no listener yet and be lost. Fixed by attaching the listener synchronously before any await.
preconditions: A connector configured to send its registration envelope the instant the WS connection opens
steps: Connect and immediately send the registration envelope in the same tick
expectedResult: The registration envelope is processed every time — never silently dropped due to listener-attachment timing.

title: The shared Evidence schema accepts sourceType 'vtec_connector' without a validation failure
preconditions: A constructed Evidence document with sourceType: 'vtec_connector' and a populated vtecConnector sub-doc
expectedResult: Validation passes with no error; status defaults to 'draft' as it does for manual_upload/ai_assisted_upload.

title: Rotator.OnRotate no longer silently discards the first subscriber when a second one registers
description: OnRotate used to be a single-slot field field; registering a second callback (needed for the cert-expiry gauge, Task 9.1) overwrote the first (websocket.Client.UpdateCertificate) with no error or warning. Fixed to a slice, invoked in registration order.
preconditions: Two OnRotate callbacks registered on the same Rotator
expectedResult: Both callbacks fire; neither silently fails to be called.
